subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or per-agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source and tests make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make operator config the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed current global or per-agent policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep durable session overrides
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing lanes.

options.title: Ship explicit reset first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make operator config the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed current global or per-agent policy, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest feature and test history for durable `/exec` session overrides points to `steipete`.
